source.title: Harmless interpolation in regression and classification with structured features
source.authors: Andrew D. McRae; Santhosh Karnik; M. Davenport; Vidya K. Muthukumar

record.file_problem: Full text supplied, including supplementary material.
record.tranche_reason: Analyzes harmless interpolation of noise in kernel regression and classification theoretically and with numerical experiments. It does not train standard deep networks or test random image labels, so it tests only a related interpolation claim with a different model and setup.
record.gate_note: The paper studies RKHS/kernel estimators on structured features, including noisy regression observations and binary labels. It does not test fully random labels, shuffled or Gaussian inputs, training-time costs, explicit regularizers' effect on random-label fitting, or a real-label-before-noise learning order. Cited findings about neural networks and other prior work are not this study's results. The numerical experiments use noisy regression targets and stochastic binary observations generated from η*, not completely random labels.
record.test_reason: The study proves risk bounds for kernel estimators and evaluates regression error and classification excess risk on Fourier features. These results concern generalization after interpolating noisy observations, not any version's specified deep-network behavior. The original neural-network finding motivates the paper but is not tested by its own results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish sufficient conditions for harmless interpolation with structured features and demonstrate classification consistency in regimes where regression is inconsistent. These are conditional kernel/RKHS results, not results about standard deep networks fitting random labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes kernel/RKHS estimators and their risk, with theoretical bounds and Fourier-feature numerical experiments; it does not use deep-network training or random-label image experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome changes with the bi-level ensemble parameters (β, r, q): both errors decrease in one setting, classification alone decreases in another, and neither decreases in the third.

fits_no_version.finding: For (β,r,q)=(2.6,0.3,0.3), both relative squared regression error and relative classification excess risk decrease with sample size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kernel estimators with structured Fourier features can improve regression and classification performance with sample size under suitable spectral conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: For (β,r,q)=(2.6,1/3,5/6), classification excess risk decreases while regression error does not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classification consistency can occur without regression consistency for interpolating kernel estimators with structured features.

fits_no_version.finding: For (β,r,q)=(2.6,0.8,0.45), neither displayed error decreases with sample size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization of these Fourier-feature kernel estimators depends on the feature-spectrum parameter regime.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2022; PMLR Volume 151 stated in text)
record.problems: The numerical results are described as trends and shown in a figure without tabulated values or error bars in the supplied text. The experiments use kernel estimators on Fourier features, not deep networks or image data.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible findings were left out. Theoretical risk bounds and asymptotic claims were not entered as empirical rows; cited prior-work findings were excluded.

untested.parts: Standard deep networks fitting completely random labels with stochastic gradient training, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Training-time comparisons between true and random labels and convergence changes with corruption fraction.
Deep-network fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily degrading test performance across a random-label-corruption sweep.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: The numerical experiments use α=10^-3 and report test-risk trends, not training-error rates. The asymptotic interpolation analysis takes α=0. Neither supplies evidence for V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test standard deep networks, image labels, completely random labeling, training error/test error at chance, or unchanged training hyperparameters.
Does not compare training time or convergence speed for true versus random labels or vary corrupted-label fraction.
Does not train on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Does not sweep random label corruption from none to all or report training and test errors over that sweep.
Does not test weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation against random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Does not examine training order or whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: kernel ridge regression estimator η̂*
rows.size_stated: n varies between 10 and 3162; d=n^β features
rows.operation_detail: Kernel ridge regression on η*(xi) plus i.i.d. N(0,1) noise using α=10^-3; evaluated relative L2 error.

conditions.value: Fourier features vℓ(x)=e^{j2πℓx}, ℓ=−d,…,d, x∈[0,1] uniform

rows.uncertainty: averaged over 100 trials; no error bar stated
rows.note: The report describes the trend but gives no numerical error values in the text.
rows.check: The decreasing regression-error trend is correctly reported but cannot establish any claim version. The measure is relative squared L2 error. Section 4 uses 2d+1 Fourier features indexed from −d to d, rather than d features.
